title: SII Vol. 14 No. 201 — Sivapuri
location_detail: On the north wall of the prakara in the Svayamprakasesvara temple
summary: This epigraph dated in the 3rd year of the king who is simply called Srivallabha without any distinguishing epithet, has, on paleographical grounds, to be attributed to the Jatavarman of that name

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 202 — Attur
location_detail: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Somanatha temple
date_text: This record dated in the 3rd year of Srivaladeva, i.e, Srivallabhadeva, has to be attributed to Jatavarman Srivallabha
summary: It registers a gift of money by Puvandi, the wife of Appippuvan, a vellala Anguttanallur in Kalattirukkai-nadu for a lamp in the temple of Somanathadeva at Arrur

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 203 — Veppilaippatti
location_detail: Round a pillar in the Gangaiamman temple
summary: This inscription is dated in the 3rd year of Srivallabhadeva and states that this pillar was put to mark the site of the bund (anaikuri) of the tank (uruni) of Irunjonadu by Araiyan Madhurantakan alias Karunilakkudi-nadalvan

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 204 — Kunnakkudi
location_detail: On a pillar on the rock-cut cave on the hill
date_text: This record dated in the 4th year of Jatavarman Srivallabhadeva is much damaged at the end
summary: Its contents cannot, therefore, be correctly

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 205 — Solapuram
location_detail: On the east wall of the mandapa in the venkatachalapati-Perumal temple
summary: This record of Jatavarman Srivallabha which is dated in the 4th regnal year is of interest as mentioning a pillaiyar or prince named Sundara-Pandyadeva, who laws camping at Arukai Kunrattur in Anma-nadu at the time of issuing this inscription

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 206 — Dalapatisamudram
location_detail: On the south wall of the shrine in the Tirunagesvara temple
date_text: This inscription dated in the 4th year of the king is engraved in slightly later script
summary: The lateness of the script may be accounted for by supposing that the earlier records were re-copied later at the time of some renovation

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 207 — Perungulam
location_detail: On the north wall of the central shrine, Tiruvaludisvara temple
date_text: This record of Jatavaran Srivallabha is dated in his 4th year; but as it is damaged after the sixth line its purport cannot be made out
summary: Perungulam had the other name of Uttamapandyanallur

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 208 — Kunnakkudi
location_detail: On the rock left of Entrance into the first cave temple
summary: This inscription dated in the 4th year of Jatavarman Srivallabha, seems to register the gift of land made tax-free in Kilkkannamngalam by Adalaiyur-nattalvan Mummudisolan Virasekharan

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 209 — Sermadevi
location_detail: On the east wall of the Dakshinamurti shrine in the Ammainatha temple
summary: Dated in the 5th year of Srivallabha who has the simple title of Tribhuvanachakravartigal only this record registers a gift of sheep by Setuvudaiyal, wife of Kuppai-Nambi, a brahmana of Seravanmahadevi-chaturvedimangalam for burning a lamp in the temple of Srikayilasamudaiya-Mahadeva in the village

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 210 — Sermadevi
location_detail: At the right entrance into the first prakara of the Ammainatha temple
summary: This record of the 5th year of the king registers a gift of sheep by Sendan Siddan for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple of Kailasamudaiyar at Seravanmahadevi-chaturvedimangalam, a brahmadeya in Mulli-nadu

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 211 — Anaimalai
location_detail: On a stone built into the floor of the platform in the shrine of the goddess in the cave-temple
date_text: Palaeographically the record may be assigned to the 12th century
summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, the beginning and end being lost

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 212 — Sermadevi
location_detail: On the wall of the Bhaktavatsala temple
summary: It is dated in the 6th year of Srivallabhadeva, and can paleographically be attributed to the king of that name who flourished in the 12th century A.D

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 213 — Sivapuri
location_detail: On the south wall of the second prakara in the Svayamprakasa temple
summary: This record which begins with the characteristic historical introduction is in the 6th year of the king-s reign, and, and registers a gift of land by Tillainayakan Tarunendusekharan of Ariya a merchant living at Aruviyur alias Nanndesipperunderuvu in Keralasinga-valanadu, for the expenses of offer

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 214 — Attur
location_detail: On the west and south walls of the central shrine in the Somanathan temple
summary: This record begins with the introduction commencing with Tirumagal Jayamagal, etc., and is dated in the 6th year of Jatavarman Srivallabhadeva

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 215 — Kuruvitturai
location_detail: On the north wall of the shrine in the Chitrarathavallabha-Perumal temple
date_text: This inscription is dated in the 7th year of Srivallabha
summary: Tiruvarangan-Perratiru, wife of Appan-Isvaran, made a gift of gold for providing offerings to the god Uyyakkondalvar set up by her in the temple of Paramasvamin who was pleased to stand in Tiruchchakkara-tirtham in Paganur-kurram

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 216 — Marandai
location_detail: On the west wall of the central shrine, Kailasanatha temple
summary: This inscription of the 7th year of Srivallabhadeva states that the stone temple of god Srikayilasamudaiyar at Maran-Tayanallur alias Vikramapandyapuram in Mulli-nadu was erected by a certain Mani Bahuvayan alias Alagiya-So-¦-¦-¦-¦..yan

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 217 — Kunnakkudi
location_detail: On the south pillar in the rock-cut cave
summary: This record dated in the  th year of the king registers a gift of 1 ma of land by Ghatti-arasan of Tirukkunrakkudi in Tenarruppokku for a flower garden to the god Tenarru-Nayakar and another piece of land to god Pillaiyar, presumably in the same temple

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 218 — Sivapuri
location_detail: On the belt of the verandah in the first prakara, Svayamprakasa temple
date_text: This record dated in the 8th year of Tribhuvanachakravartin Srivallabhadeva has to be assigned to this king Jatavarman Srivallabha
summary: It registers that Danadan Pagaivenra-kandan alias Tuvarapativelan made a gift of land by name Anjadakanda-Navalkulam by purchase, for the kitchen expenses of the temple at Tiruttandonrisvaram-Udaiyar at Nripasekhara-chaturvedimangalam, a brahmadeya in Keralasinga-valanadu

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 219 — Kunnakkudi
location_detail: On the verandah of the north wall of the rock-cut cave
date_text: This record, which is dated in the 19th year of Srivallabhadeva, may be assigned to this king
summary: It registers a gift of land by Nattan Adavi of Tirukkunrakkudi in penatruppokku in Keralasinga-valanadu for burning a lamp in the temple of Tirumalai-udaiya Nayanar, apparently the god in the rock-cut temple

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 220 — Tiruvalisvaram
location_detail: On the south wall of the Valisvara temple
summary: This mutilated epigraph belongs to the same king and contains the regnal year 9. It mentions a previous donation of Sundara-Pandyadeva, and registers a grant of 2 makkani of land for providing sandal paste and camphor to god Tiruvalisvaram-Udaiyar

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 221 — Solapuram
location_detail: On the east wall of the Venkatachalapati temple
date_text: This record of the king, which is dated in the 9th year, furnishes a few incomplete astronomical details
summary: It is much damaged and seems to mention that the king was seated on the seat Pandiyarajan in the hall called Alagiya-Pandiyan-kudam in the palace at Madurai

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 224 — Kuruvitturai
location_detail: On the south wall of the Chitrarathavallabha-perumal temple
summary: This record does not contain the name of the king but purports to have been issued by the god himself, who is called Sarngin of Chakratirtham ; but it may be attributed to the time of Jatavarman Srivallabha because a new channel with the name of Sri-Vallabhapperaru is mentioned as having been dug to

title: SII Vol. 14 No. 225 — Rajasingamangalam
location_detail: On the north, west and south walls of the Kailsanathasvamin temple
